correctness.rationale: For n=3^a m, gcd(m,3)=1, the normalized derivative is a/3+∑_{p^e∥m}e/p and normalized totient is (2/3)∏_{p|m}(1−1/p). If m>1, a≥2 contradicts strict bound <2/3; any even m likewise forces a strictly larger derivative than totient. With a=1, n=3m, D(n)=m+3D(m)≡m ≠0 mod 3; equality with 2φ(m) forces no factor p≡1 mod3 in m. All remaining p≡−1 mod3, and reducing m≡2φ(m) mod3 gives (−1)^ω(m)=−1, hence odd support, excluding total support exactly three. m=1 gives n=9, while for m=p^b solve 1/3+b/p=(2/3)(p−1)/p yielding p=3b+2 exactly. A fresh direct sieve through 30000 for every multiple of 3 found hits 9,15,3993, all with required profile. The modular proof, not finite sieve, proves unrestricted exponents.

value.rationale: The natural D(n)=φ(n) Diophantine problem has nontrivial infinite prime-power families; this inexpensive but complete unbounded prime-3 local sieve rules out all 3-supported solutions containing 3 and constrains residue and distinct-support parity in every larger case. It is a motivated structural obstruction rather than a single small counterexample. It does not purport to classify the full equation.
